newsitem.title: INDIA: Survivors of India fire search among corpses.
newsitem.headline: Survivors of India fire search among corpses.

text.p: Survivors of a searing fire that killed at least 182 worshippers at a Hindu rite in eastern India searched desperately on Monday for missing relatives among charred bodies.

"Women searched frantically because they did not know if their male relatives were alive," said P.K. Barik, a 46-year-old devotee who survived Sunday's blaze and was recovering in a hospital in nearby Cuttack town.

"Relatives were crying desperately, looking for any information from police," said Sandeep Sahu, a journalist who visited the site of the fire in Baripada town, 220 km (135 miles) north of the capital of Orissa state, Bhubaneshwar.

Blackened bodies lay in a row at the makeshift camp site where at least 158 devotees were burnt alive on Sunday when flames tore through a cluster of makeshift bamboo and straw shelters, packed with napping worshippers.
"It looks like a burial ground with dead bodies littered all over," said P.K. Mishra, deputy police chief of Baripada town where the inferno struck on Sunday.
Only about 33 of the bodies at the camp site had been identified and tagged by Monday morning, rescuers said. Relatives and rescuers searched for watches and rings among the mangled bodies and ashes.
Doctors struggled to save dozens of badly burned victims, who were among 15,000 devotees attending the three-day rite.
"At the moment more than 100 doctors are working on the patients," Dr Binoy Kumar Aggarwal of District Headquarters Hospital in Baripada told Reuters.
The inferno erupted on the last day of a convention dedicated to a Hindu guru in Baripada, about 220 km (135 miles) north of the capital of Orissa state, Bhubaneshwar.
Aggarwal said 24 of 187 injured died in hospital. About a dozen others were in serious condition in the Baripada hospital with burns to over 70 to 80 percent of their bodies.

Another 24 patients in very serious condition had been shifted to a hospital in Cuttack, about 175 km (110 miles) southwest of Baripada, Aggarwal said. At least 50 doctors had rushed to Baripada headquarters hospital to complement the resident team of a similar number.

The flames, fanned by gusting winds, scorched the shelters for men devotees but spared a separate section for women and children. The cause of the fire was thought to be a short circuit or gas cylinder that exploded.
"There was hardly any time to escape as the fire burnt down the camp within three minutes," said 27-year-old Dilip Kumar Mohapatra, who was recovering in a Cuttack hospital.
"There was a near stampede because everyone was trying to get out of the only gate."

Most of the victims were men taking a siesta after lunch at the annual national convention, dedicated to the memory of the Hindu guru Nigamananda, state home (interior) minister S.C. Hota said. "The number of exits at the camp was very limited," he said. "That was a problem."
Straw had been spread on the ground to serve as bedding. The temperature in the region was 32 degrees Celsius (90 Fahrenheit) and the weather was dry.
"Accommodation for the delegates was made almost entirely of straw," survivor Bhagbal Sahu said. "That made it easier for the fire to spread and hardly allowed people any time to get out."
